title: Clean backup
intro: Backups are kept in Borg repositories, one folder per virtual machine inside a backup storage. This page deletes the old backups and the repositories of machines that no longer exist, storage by storage.
readOnly: Only an administrator can change these settings or start a cleaning.
unableLoad: Unable to load the cleaning settings
unableScan: Unable to look for the machines that no longer exist

automatic.title: Automatic cleaning
automatic.warning: "Keep one backup per day for the last N days" means that one backup per day is kept for the last N days and everything older is deleted. The weekly and monthly retention of the backup policies is not taken into account: those older backups are deleted too. Borg counts the days that have a backup: a machine that was not backed up for a month keeps its last backups. Only the last backup of each of those days is kept, and the oldest backup is not kept apart.
automatic.keepDays: Keep one backup per day for the last N days
automatic.afterBackup: Clean the repository of a machine right after its backup
automatic.scheduled: Run a cleaning on a schedule
automatic.cron: Cron expression (minute hour day month weekday)
automatic.cronInvalid: This is not a valid cron expression
automatic.hook: Notify this Slack hook (start, end, failure)
automatic.keepDaysExample: Example with 3 days: a machine backed up on the 1st, 5th, 10th and 20th of the month keeps the last backup of the 5th, 10th and 20th. The one of the 1st is deleted.
automatic.lowDays: With only {days} day(s) kept, a damaged last backup leaves nothing older to restore from. At least 3 days is advised.

run.title: Run now
run.help: Applies the rule above to every repository of the storage: in each one, the last backup of each of the N most recent days that have a backup is kept, and the others are deleted. Start with the simulation to see, and choose, what would be deleted.
run.confirm: Apply the rule “last backup of each of the {days} most recent days with a backup” to {storage}? The other backups are deleted. This cannot be undone.
run.failed: The cleaning failed, see the history for details
run.unsaved: The number of days was changed but not saved. Save it first: the simulation and the cleaning use the saved value.

orphans.title: Backups of machines that no longer exist
orphans.help: Looks in the storage for repositories whose machine is not known by any hypervisor anymore. Nothing is deleted until you select the repositories and confirm.
orphans.scanning: Looking for the machines that no longer exist…
orphans.none: No backup of a machine that no longer exists was found.
orphans.machines: {count} machine exists in the hypervisors. | {count} machines exist in the hypervisors.

orphans.deleteIntro: These repositories and all their backups will be deleted. This cannot be undone:

simulation.days: Simulation with the saved number of days: {days}. Nothing is deleted by it.
simulation.none: Nothing would be deleted: the rule keeps every backup.
simulation.hint: Everything is ticked: untick what you want to keep, then delete the selection. A backup left unticked is only kept until another cleaning applies the rule (scheduled, after a backup, or “Run the cleaning”).
